tests.title: Every operation in the event tables records exactly its documented event
given: a deployment able to perform every operation the two event tables name
tests.when: each operation is performed in turn and the recorded events are read
then: each records exactly one event
each event's type and action match the table
each event's metadata keys are exactly those the table lists, with no extra key
the actor is the calling credential's user and type, or the system actor where the table says so
tests.pseudocode: in the event recorder integration test file, driven from a table transcribed from the reference: perform(op); e = latest_event(); assert (e.event_type, e.action) == expected and set(e.metadata) == expected_keys

tests.title: A failing recorder does not change any request's answer
given: an event recorder made to raise on every call
tests.when: a representative operation from each event-recording package is performed, successfully and in a refused form
then: every status and body matches the answer given with the recorder working
no request fails because of the recorder
tests.pseudocode: in the event recorder test file: for op in OPS: a = run(op, recorder=ok); b = run(op, recorder=raising); assert a.status == b.status and a.json == b.json

tests.title: A bound token's refusals are recorded at most once a minute with the rest counted
given: a bound token and a controllable clock
tests.when: the token is refused twenty times within a minute, then once more after the minute has passed
then: exactly one event is recorded for the first twenty
its suppressed count is nineteen
the refusal after the minute records a second event
tests.pseudocode: in the event recorder integration test file: for _ in range(20): refuse(); assert len(events()) == 1 and events()[0].metadata.suppressed == 19; clock.advance(61); refuse(); assert len(events()) == 2

tests.title: Workspace-less events reach admin tokens only
given: recorded events that belong to no workspace and events of a workspace the caller owns
tests.when: the unified query and the stream are read by a user and by an admin token
then: the user receives only the workspace events
the admin token receives both
the same holds for the stream
tests.pseudocode: in the audit query test file: assert all(e.workspace for e in query(user)) and any(not e.workspace for e in query(admin))

tests.title: Each per-run record is ingested once and a repeat is a duplicate
given: a workspace the caller owns and a valid run id
tests.when: an audit event, a session outcome, a tool call, a tool error and a trace event are each ingested, and each is then ingested again with the same id
then: each first ingestion answers 201 with the record's identity
each repeat answers 200 and stores no second record
each record is afterwards returned by its run's list route
tests.pseudocode: in the ingestion integration test file, table over the five record kinds asserting 201 then 200 and a count of one

tests.title: Malformed run ids, timestamps and fields are refused
given: a workspace the caller owns
tests.when: ingestions are made with a run id of the wrong shape, with uppercase hex, with a malformed timestamp, with an invalid severity, and with a required field missing
then: each answers 400
no record is stored for any of them
a batch's failing item is reported by its index while the others are stored
tests.pseudocode: in the ingestion test file, table over the malformed inputs asserting 400 and the stored count

tests.title: Ingestion checks the workspace, then that it is not archived, then ownership
given: an owned active workspace, an owned archived one, a workspace the caller is only a member of, one they cannot see, and a slug naming nothing
tests.when: each ingestion route is called against each, including a member against an archived workspace
then: the unknown and invisible workspaces answer 404
the archived workspace answers 409 workspace_archived, including for a member, because the status is checked before ownership
a member or stranger of an active workspace answers 403 workspace_access_denied, not 404
no record is stored for any refusal
tests.pseudocode: in the ingestion test file, table over (caller, workspaceStatus, expectedStatus, expectedErrorType)

tests.title: A batch reports accepted, duplicate and failing items separately
given: a run with some records already ingested
tests.when: a batch of 100 items is sent of which 3 repeat existing ids and 2 are malformed, then an empty array, then a batch of 1001 items
then: the batch answers 200 with 95 accepted, 3 duplicates and 2 errors naming their indices
the 95 valid items are stored despite the failures
the empty array answers 400 and the oversized batch answers 413
tests.pseudocode: in the ingestion integration test file: r = post(batch); assert (r.json.accepted, r.json.duplicates, len(r.json.errors)) == (95, 3, 2)

tests.title: A run has exactly one postmortem
given: a run with no postmortem
tests.when: a postmortem is submitted and then a different one is submitted for the same run
then: the first answers 201 with the run id, the run status and the time stored
the second answers 200
the stored postmortem is the first one
tests.pseudocode: in the postmortem integration test file: a = post(pm1); b = post(pm2); assert a.status == 201 and b.status == 200 and get(pm).json.run_status == pm1.run_status

tests.title: A malformed postmortem is refused and a missing one is reported
given: a run with no postmortem
tests.when: postmortems are submitted with a missing required field, an invalid run status, an invalid time and a schema version of 2, and the postmortem of a run without one is read
then: the missing field and the invalid status and time answer 400
the schema version answers 422 with error_type unknown_schema_version
the read answers 404 with error_type postmortem_not_found
nothing is stored
tests.pseudocode: in the postmortem test file, table over the four submissions plus the read asserting the statuses and error types

tests.title: A run's records are listed with their filters and paging
given: a run with records of each kind across several nodes, sessions, types and times
tests.when: each list route is read with no filter, with each documented filter, in both orders, and with page sizes of 1, 50 and 501
then: each answers 200 with its named collection, next_cursor and has_more
the default order is newest first and the default page size 50, capped at 500
each filter narrows the result to the matching records
tests.pseudocode: in the run reads integration test file, table over (route, filter) asserting the returned ids

tests.title: A run's records are readable by the owner, a member and an admin token whatever the status
given: an active and an archived workspace with run records, and the owner, a member, a stranger and an admin token
tests.when: each list route is read by each caller against each workspace
then: the owner, the member and the admin token are served for both workspaces
the stranger is answered 404 workspace not found
tests.pseudocode: in the run reads test file, table over (caller, workspaceStatus, expected)

tests.title: A run read with a bad run id, cursor or time is refused
given: a readable workspace
tests.when: each list route is read with a malformed run id, an invalid cursor, a malformed since and an until before the since
then: each answers 400 in the error envelope
tests.pseudocode: in the run reads test file, table over (route, badParameter) asserting 400

tests.title: Hub and agent events interleave by instant
given: hub events and agent events recorded alternately, some within the same second and with differing fractional precision
tests.when: the unified query is read and paged to the end
then: the events are returned newest first by instant across both sources
events of the same second are ordered by their fractional parts
paging to the end yields every event exactly once
tests.pseudocode: in the audit query integration test file: all = read_all_pages(); assert [e.timestamp for e in all] == sorted(timestamps, reverse=True)

tests.title: A source-specific filter excludes the other source
given: hub events and agent events for one workspace
tests.when: the query is read with source hub, source agent, actor_id, actor_type, resource_type, action, run_id, event_type and event_type_prefix
then: actor_id, actor_type, resource_type and action return only hub events
run_id returns only agent events
source selects one source directly
event_type and its prefix narrow within whichever sources remain
tests.pseudocode: in the audit query test file, table over (filter, expectedSources)

tests.title: The query returns the caller's workspaces whatever their status
given: events of a workspace the caller owns, one of an archived workspace they own, one of a workspace they share an organization with, one of a workspace they cannot see, and workspace-less events
tests.when: the query is read by the user and by an admin token
then: the user receives the owned, archived and shared workspaces' events
the user receives neither the invisible workspace's nor the workspace-less events
the admin token receives all of them
tests.pseudocode: in the audit query integration test file: assert workspaces(query(user)) == {owned, archived, shared}

tests.title: A bad query is refused
given: a readable workspace and one the caller cannot read
tests.when: the query is read with an invalid cursor, a malformed time, a since equal to and after the until, and naming the unreadable workspace
then: the cursor, the time and the inverted period answer 400
the unreadable workspace answers 404 workspace not found
tests.pseudocode: in the audit query test file, table over the four cases asserting the status

tests.title: A transcript is rebuilt from a node's traces
given: a run whose node has trace events of every type, in a known order, plus traces of another node
tests.when: the transcript is requested for that node
then: the messages are in the traces' order
a session init is a system message, an assistant message an assistant message, a tool use a tool_use message with its tool name, and a tool error a tool_error message
trace types outside those four produce no message
the other node's traces do not appear
tests.pseudocode: in the transcript integration test file: r = get(transcript, node_id=n); assert [m.role for m in r.json.messages] == expected

tests.title: A transcript without a node is refused
given: a run with traces
tests.when: the transcript is requested with no node and with an empty node
then: each answers 400 in the error envelope
tests.pseudocode: in the transcript test file: assert get(transcript).status == 400 and get(transcript, node_id='').status == 400

tests.title: The stream opens with a heartbeat and keeps beating
given: a readable workspace and a controllable clock
tests.when: a client opens the stream and waits past two heartbeat intervals while an event is recorded
then: the response is 200 with Content-Type text/event-stream
a heartbeat frame arrives immediately
further heartbeats arrive at 30-second intervals
the recorded event arrives as its own frame
tests.pseudocode: in the event stream integration test file: s = open(stream); assert s.next().event == 'heartbeat'; clock.advance(30); assert s.next().event == 'heartbeat'

tests.title: A silent client is disconnected and a slow one loses the oldest events
given: a client that stops reading, and one that reads slowly while 300 events are recorded
tests.when: 60 seconds pass for the first, and the second is allowed to drain
then: the silent client's connection is closed after 60 seconds
the slow client receives the most recent 256 events and loses the oldest
the service's memory does not grow without bound in either case
tests.pseudocode: in the event stream integration test file: stop_reading(); clock.advance(61); assert closed(s); assert len(drain(slow)) == 256

tests.title: A stream's visible workspaces are fixed when it opens
given: a user streaming the events of the organizations they belong to
tests.when: the user is added to another organization and removed from one, while the stream is open, and events are recorded for both
then: the open stream's visible set does not change
a new connection reflects the new membership
tests.pseudocode: in the event stream integration test file: s = open(stream); change_membership(); assert visible(s) == before; assert visible(open(stream)) == after

tests.title: An event recorded by another component reaches the stream
given: two instances of the service over one platform, with a stream served by the first
tests.when: the second instance records an event for the subscribed workspace
then: the subscriber receives the event
it does so without reconnecting
the same holds with the two instances swapped
tests.pseudocode: in the event stream integration test file: s = instanceA.open(stream); instanceB.record(event); assert s.next().data.id == event.id

tests.title: An unreadable workspace and the connection limit are refused
given: a workspace the caller cannot read and a service at its configured stream limit
tests.when: a stream is opened for the unreadable workspace and another at the limit
then: the unreadable workspace answers 404 before any frame is sent
the limit answers 503
neither leaves a half-open stream
tests.pseudocode: in the event stream test file: assert open(stream, foreign).status == 404 and open(stream).status == 503 at the limit

tests.title: An archive is recorded and found through the query
given: a running deployment and a ready workspace
tests.when: the workspace is archived and the unified query is read for it
then: the archive succeeds
exactly one workspace archive event is returned, with the caller as actor
its metadata keys are those the reference lists
tests.pseudocode: in the audit smoke test file: post(archive); e = query(workspace=slug).json.events[0]; assert e.event_type == 'hub.workspace.archive'

tests.title: A run is ingested and read back against a running deployment
given: a running deployment and a workspace the caller owns
tests.when: a batch of traces with some repeated ids is ingested, a postmortem is submitted, and the traces, the postmortem and one node's transcript are read
then: the batch reports the accepted and duplicate counts
the postmortem is returned as submitted
the transcript's messages are rebuilt from the ingested traces in order
tests.pseudocode: in the audit smoke test file: post(traces_batch); post(postmortem); assert get(transcript, node_id=n).json.messages

tests.title: A watcher receives an event recorded elsewhere in the deployment
given: a running deployment serving more than one instance, and a readable workspace
tests.when: a stream is opened for the workspace and an operation on another instance records an event for it
then: the stream delivers a heartbeat at once
the event arrives as its own frame without reconnection
the event's id matches the one recorded
tests.pseudocode: in the audit smoke test file: s = open(stream); trigger_event_elsewhere(); assert s.next_event().id == recorded.id
